rating.reasoning_summary: This strand represents a **Dialectical Exploration** of IQ as a boundary object, beginning with Eigenrobot's viral prompt to "poast IQ cowards" (April 2021) and evolving through multiple phases: (1) Initial reveal/vulnerability (people posting their scores), (2) Yashkaf's intervention framing IQ as privilege/obligation, (3) Absurdist derailment (Eigenrobot's "dong measurement" joke spawning Ultimape's multi-year biological research tangent), and (4) Long-tail critique (2025 tweets questioning IQ's validity as intelligence measure). The strand demonstrates both **constructive knowledge production** (Yashkaf's privilege framework, Ultimape's hedgehog signaling discoveries) and **dialectical tension** (high-IQ rationalists simultaneously claiming "IQ doesn't matter" while being defined by it). The Ultimape tangent—though comedic—represents genuine scientific curiosity cascading from a shitpost into legitimate endocrinology research, exemplifying the community's "follow the weirdness" ethos.

title: “Post IQ, cowards” turned into hedgehog dick science
summary: But the funniest aftershock is @eigenrobot trying to defuse the IQ dick-measuring contest by literally making it a dick-measuring contest—“poast dong measurement cowards”—which @ultimape takes as a research prompt and spins into a months/years-long horny-science jag about Sonic Hedgehog signaling, echidna genitals, erectile function papers, and inventing a “Penis Cup” apparatus. Years later the long-tail re-litigates the original question: @lemondotpng/@lemonaut1 argues “IQ fails to capture ‘real’ intelligence,” @zagrebbi says IQ guys are cringe because it’s often compensation for broken executive function, and @DefenderOfBasic tries to synthesize it: yes intelligence is partly fixed, but most people are “dumber than they could be” due to missing motivation/purpose. Why care? It’s a perfect snapshot of internet rationalists’ core contradiction: obsessed with measurement/status while insisting it doesn’t matter—until someone forces them to admit what it buys, or the whole thing veers into absurdist bio-research because that’s safer than talking about hierarchy directly.
